1.

Petitioner is before this Court assailing the order dated 02.07.2024 passed by the Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bidar, in Crime No.66/2023 wherein B Report filed by the Bidar Women Police Station, Bidar, has been accepted and case registered against respondent was closed.

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

FIR in Crime No.66/2023 was registered by Bidar Women Police Station, Bidar, against respondent herein for the offence punishable under Section 354(A)(3) of IPC and Sections 8, 11(iii)
and 12 of POCSO Act, 2012, on the basis of the first information received from respondent No.2 herein.

Police after investigation have filed B final report in the said case and respondent Sadhana vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 1 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116174125/
2 No.2/defacto complainant had given her no objection to accept the said B final report.

entities.text: respondent Sadhana vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However,
acceptance of B final report was protested by the petitioner herein, who is the mother of alleged victim girl by filing a detailed protest petition dated 11.03.2024.

Learned Trial Court vide the order impugned dated 02.07.2024 after considering the contentions urged on behalf of the petitioner,
being satisfied with the B final report filed in the present case, has accepted the same and closed the case as against the respondent.
Being aggrieved by the same, this petition is filed.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the reasons assigned by the learned Trial Judge for accepting the B final report is not proper.
He also submits that merely for the reason that there was a dispute between the parents of the victim girl, the version of the victim girl cannot be doubted.

He NC: 2025:KHC-K:749 submits that victim girl has made specific allegations against respondent/accused which would attract the alleged offences and therefore, police could not have filed B report in the present case.
The Trial Court has failed to appreciate this aspect of the matter and has erred in accepting the B report.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3/accused submits that there are multiple proceedings pending between the petitioner and respondent No.3.
Police have collected necessary material during the course of investigation and having appreciated the same, have rightly filed B final report in the present case.
Since foundational facts of the case is defective, no presumption can be raised in the present case as against the accused.
He submits that petitioner had made a demand for payment of Rs.2 crore 50 lakhs which is on record and had threatened to file false criminal case against the accused.
Necessary material to prove such demand made by the petitioner was furnished to the police during the course of investigation and such material is part of the charge sheet.
The Trial Court having appreciated all these aspects of the matter has rightly accepted the B final report.

He submits that only NC: 2025:KHC-K:749 with an intention to wreck vengeance at the instance of the petitioner, criminal proceedings for the alleged offences in the present case was initiated and in similar circumstances, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ahmad Ali Quraishi and Another vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another reported in (2020) 13 SCC 435, has quashed the criminal proceedings.
6.

entities.text: Ahmad Ali Quraishi and Another vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another reported in (2020) 13 SCC 435
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner herein claims to be the wife of the accused/respondent No.3.
Victim is the daughter of petitioner from her first marriage.

FIR in Crime No.66/2023 was registered against respondent No.3 for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 03.11.2023 received from respondent No.2, who was working as Superintendent of Government Girls Home, Mailoor in Bidar District.

In the first information, it is stated that victim girl, who is the daughter of petitioner,
studying in 10th Std informed that when she was studying in 6th Std, accused used to show her obscene videos in his mobile phone and on 09.08.2023 at about 12.00 a.m. in the mid night, he had sexually assaulted her.

Though, it is alleged in the first information that on 09.08.2023, accused had sexually assaulted the victim girl, during the course of NC: 2025:KHC-K:749 recording the statement of the victim girl, she had not stated the exact date on which she was sexually assaulted by the accused.

7. The material on record would go to show that petitioner herein had earlier filed O.S.No.6/2022 before the jurisdictional Family Court against the accused with a prayer to declare that she is his Sadhana vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 1 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116174125/
3 wife and also to grant decree restraining him from contracting a second marriage.

sentences.text:
She also had filed a criminal case against respondent No.3/accused in Crime No.65/2023 for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 323, 504, 506 and 149 of IPC and in the said case, police after investigation,
have filed a 'B'-final report on 20.06.2023.
The decree which was passed in O.S.No.6/2022 has been questioned by respondent No.3 in MFA No.202785/2023 which is pending consideration before this Court.

8. Petitioner herein had initiated separate proceedings on 20.07.2023 before the jurisdictional Court against respondent No.3 under the provisions of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act in Crl.Misc.No.644/2023 and in the said proceedings, she has specifically pleaded that from the month NC: 2025:KHC-K:749 of February, 2022 onwards respondent has not been visiting her house and she was also not receiving her phone calls.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The allegation now made in the first information is that respondent No.3 had sexually assaulted the victim girl on 09.08.2023.

If the statement made in the proceedings under Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, which was filed in the month of July, 2023, is correct, then it is difficult to believe the allegations found in the first information against respondent No.3 that he had sexually assaulted the victim girl on the night of 09.08.2023.
9.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The police during the course of investigation in the present case have collected material which is the subject matter of PF No.00/2023 as mentioned in the charge sheet which relates to demand made by petitioner with respondent No.3 for payment of Rs.2 crores 50 lakhs towards settlement failing which she has threatened to send him to jail.
The demand made by petitioner is also recorded in audio clipping which is also part of the charge sheet.
According to the petitioner, the victim girl had suffered the alleged act committed by respondent No.3 in silence and she had not revealed the same to her.
She had for the first time revealed NC: 2025:KHC-K:749 the same to her sister Premakumari who also is working as Head Mistress in the School in which the victim girl is studying.
In the B Final Report, it is mentioned that petitioner and Premakumari had another sister by name Jyothi, who was married to Veerendra.

After the death of Jyothi, Premakumari had initiated proceedings before the jurisdictional Court at Bidar against Veerendra contending that she was the wife of Veerendra and had made a claim for custody of his children in G & WC No.5/2022.
The jurisdictional Court had dismissed her claim and a copy of the order passed in G & WC No.5/2022 is also part of the B report filed before the Trial Court.

10. In the background of various litigation which were filed prior to FIR registered in the present case and also having regard to material made available to the Investigation Officer by respondent No.3 during investigation, which would prima facie reveal that a demand was made by the petitioner for payment of Rs.2 crores 50 lakhs failing which she had threatened to send him to jail, police after investigating have filed B final report in the present case.
A perusal of the B final report would go to show that the same is filed after extensively investigating the matter and after collecting all the necessary NC: 2025:KHC-K:749 material.

The Trial Court therefore, having appreciated the contents of the B report has rightly accepted the same and closed the case against respondent No.3.
11.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ahmad Ali Quraishi and Another (supra), in a case where criminal case was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 354, 504, 506 Sadhana vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 1 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116174125/
4 and 452 of IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act, taking into consideration that parities were fighting various litigation between themselves earlier and therefore, criminal proceedings was initiated only to wreck vengeance against the accused, has quashed similar criminal proceedings.

sentences.text: In the case on hand, Investigation Officer having held a detailed investigation has filed B final report and the contents of the B final report would go to show that Investigation Officer was justified in submitting the same.
Under the circumstances, I do not find any good ground to entertain this petition.
Accordingly, petition is dismissed.
